title: Conjecture 1.1 (Dallard, Milanič and Štorgel)
statement_text: A class $\mathcal{C}$ of graphs is $(\operatorname{tw},\omega)$-bounded if and only if it has bounded $\operatorname{tree-\alpha}$.
context_text: A graph class $\mathcal{G}$ is called $(\operatorname{tw},\omega)$-bounded if there exists a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that for every graph $G\in\mathcal{G}$ and every induced subgraph $H$ of $G$, $\operatorname{tw}(H)\leq f(\omega(H))$. By Ramsey's theorem, graph classes of bounded tree independence number are $(\operatorname{tw},\omega)$-bounded, but the converse is open. The conjecture would settle whether the $(\operatorname{tw},\omega)$-bounded property has algorithmic implications for the MWIS problem.
paper_contribution: Proves that the class $\mathcal{C}$ of (even hole, diamond, pyramid)-free graphs has bounded $\operatorname{tree-\alpha}$, corroborating the conjecture for this class (which was already known to be $(\operatorname{tw},\omega)$-bounded).
paper_title: Tree independence number I. (Even hole, diamond, pyramid)-free graphs

title: Conjecture 1.6
statement_text: The class of (even hole, diamond)-free graph has bounded tree-$\alpha$.
context_text: A hole is an induced cycle of length at least 4, and it is even if its length is even; a class is ($H_1,H_2,\dots$)-free if no graph in it contains any $H_i$ as an induced subgraph (for holes: no even hole as an induced subgraph). A diamond is $K_4$ minus an edge. A pyramid consists of a vertex $a$, a triangle $b_1b_2b_3$ disjoint from $a$, and three paths $P_1,P_2,P_3$ from $a$ to $b_1,b_2,b_3$ such that any two of them induce a hole (so at least two of them have length at least 2). The independence number of a tree decomposition is the maximum independence number $\alpha$ of the subgraph induced by a bag, and the tree independence number tree-$\alpha(G)$ is the minimum of this over all tree decompositions of $G$. Graphs of bounded tree-$\alpha$ admit polynomial-time algorithms for Maximum Weight Independent Set (MWIS), and bounded tree-$\alpha$ implies that treewidth is bounded by a function of the clique number $\omega$ in every induced subgraph ($(\mathrm{tw},\omega)$-boundedness); Dallard, Milanič and Štorgel conjectured that the converse holds for hereditary classes. The paper's main result is that the class of ($C_4$, diamond, theta, pyramid, prism, even wheel)-free graphs, which contains all (even hole, diamond, pyramid)-free graphs, has bounded tree-$\alpha$, yielding a polynomial-time MWIS algorithm and confirming the Dallard–Milanič–Štorgel conjecture for this class. The conjecture drops the pyramid-free condition. (Even hole, diamond)-free graphs are known to be colourable in polynomial time (via a decomposition by star cutsets and 2-joins showing they always have a simplicial vertex or a vertex of degree 2), but no polynomial-time MWIS algorithm is yet known for them; the authors believe their central-bag method may extend to this class. Allowing pyramids destroys the polynomial bound on the number of minimal separators used in some earlier approaches.

title: Conjecture 1.7
statement_text: The class of (even hole, $K_{t}$)-free graph has logarithmic treewidth.
context_text: A hole is an induced cycle of length at least 4, and it is even if its length is even; a class is ($H_1,H_2,\dots$)-free if no graph in it contains any $H_i$ as an induced subgraph (for holes: no even hole as an induced subgraph). A diamond is $K_4$ minus an edge. A pyramid consists of a vertex $a$, a triangle $b_1b_2b_3$ disjoint from $a$, and three paths $P_1,P_2,P_3$ from $a$ to $b_1,b_2,b_3$ such that any two of them induce a hole (so at least two of them have length at least 2). A class has logarithmic treewidth if (in the usual sense, not spelled out in the paper) there is a constant $c$ such that every $n$-vertex graph in the class has treewidth at most $c\log n$; here $t$ is fixed and the constant may depend on $t$. It is known (Cameron et al.) that (even hole, $K_3$)-free graphs have treewidth at most 5, whereas the layered wheel construction shows that (even hole, $K_4$)-free graphs have unbounded treewidth; layered wheels contain many diamonds, and (even hole, diamond, $K_4$)-free graphs, and more generally even-hole-free graphs excluding a clique and a certain family of graphs containing diamonds, have bounded treewidth. Also, for each $t$, (even hole, diamond, pyramid, $K_t$)-free graphs have bounded treewidth. Logarithmic treewidth is known to hold if one additionally forbids the family of generalized $k$-pyramids, and a forthcoming paper of some of the authors works towards logarithmic treewidth for even-hole-free graphs.
